title: "5. More Experiments, Easier Targets"

## **Why Multivariate Normal Distributions?**

[Explain why controlled distributions are useful.]

## **The Experimental Strategy**

We systematically vary:

- dimensionality,
- variance structure,
- correlation structure,
- anisotropy,
- coordinate representation.

The main quantities of interest are:

- warmup length,
- nested $\widehat{R}$,
- mean squared error.

<div class="plot-panel">
  <img id="cov-plot" src="../figures/chapter05/bivariate/cov1_1.png" alt="Bivariate covariance plot">

<script>
let currentConfig = '1-1';

function fileStem(config) {
  return '../figures/chapter05/bivariate/cov' + config.replace(/-/g, '_');
}

function renderPlot() {
  document.getElementById('cov-plot').src = fileStem(currentConfig) + '.png';
}

function showPlot(config) {
  currentConfig = config;
  renderPlot();
}

document.querySelectorAll('.cov-btn').forEach(btn => {
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => showPlot(btn.dataset.config));
});

// Optional: highlight the active button
document.querySelectorAll('.cov-btn').forEach(btn => {
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.cov-btn').forEach(b => b.classList.remove('active'));
    btn.classList.add('active');
  });
});
</script>

## **What Are We Looking For?**

We are looking for the connection between the MSE vs. $\widehat{R}_{\nu}$ on different distributions.
